title: Kilometer-Scale AI-Powered and Performance-Portable Earth System Model (AP3ESM) to Achieve Year-Scale Simulation Speed on Heterogeneous Supercomputers
problem: Ultra-high-resolution Earth system models (ESMs) at kilometer scale require exascale resources; achieving performance portability across heterogeneous architectures is challenging.
method: AP3ESM: Kokkos/OpenMP performance-portable implementation with AI-enhanced physical parameterizations, adaptive algorithms, and mixed-precision on Sunway and GPU systems.

title: Comparison-Free Bit-Stream Generation for Cost-Efficient Unary Computing
problem: Converting binary radix data to unary representation via comparator-based generators incurs high area and power cost, especially as input count and precision increase.
method: Proposes low-cost comparison-free unary number generation mechanism avoiding comparators entirely. Introduces serial and two parallel (exact and approximate) unary generator designs using alternative conversion logic.

title: 20.9 An Autonomous and Lightweight Microactuator Driving System Using Flying Solid-State Batteries
problem: Small-scale flying electromechanical systems (microrobotics) require efficient high-voltage drive systems for electrostatic and piezoelectric actuators while meeting stringent weight (<1-2g) and power constraints for flight endurance (10s of minutes).
method: The system manages reactive energy delivery to capacitive loads by using flying solid-state batteries that enable integrated power conversion from low-voltage sources (3-5V) to high voltages (tens of volts), optimizing the voltage conversion ratio and reactive power efficiency.

title: BirdMoE: Reducing Communication Costs for Mixture-of-Experts Training Using Load-Aware Bi-random Quantization
problem: MoE model parallelism in LLM training (e.g., ChatGPT) faces intensive all-to-all collective communication of intermediate results between expert nodes, substantially degrading training efficiency.
method: BirdMoE proposes load-aware communication compression with bi-random quantization: (1) Random Quantization maps floating-point intermediate results to integers with expectation invariance preserving training quality, and (2) Mixed Precision strategy dynamically balances communication loads among expert nodes to improve all-to-all communication efficiency.

title: Enhancing HPX with FleCSI: Automatic Detection of Implicit Task Dependencies
problem: Mapping Legion-like task graph programming model to HPX's different programming semantics is challenging; balancing parallelism opportunities vs overhead
method: Design and implement HPX backend for FleCSI; map task dependencies to HPX futures; optimize inter-task communicator creation to minimize costly operations; empirical evaluation on two physics applications

title: CVMAX: Accelerator Architecture with Polar Form Multiplication for Complex-Valued Neural Networks
problem: Complex-Valued Neural Networks (CVNNs) suffer from higher computational and memory overheads than real-valued networks but are essential for applications using complex numbers; deploying CVNNs on resource-constrained devices requires energy and area optimization.
method: CVMAX is a software-hardware co-design using specialized quantization based on polar form representation (magnitude and phase) combined with shift quantization. Polar form reduces bit width and computational complexity significantly versus rectangular form. A dedicated hardware accelerator supports CVMAX data types and arithmetic operations optimized for polar multiplication simplicity.

title: GreenMix: Energy-Efficient Serverless Computing via Randomized Sketching on Asymmetric Multi-Cores
problem: Serverless computing on asymmetric multi-core processors (big.LITTLE, Alder Lake) presents optimization challenges for energy efficiency and keep-alive costs while maintaining QoS targets.
method: GreenMix uses randomized sketching algorithm tailored for serverless execution to optimally assign functions to core types. Targets energy minimization and keep-alive cost reduction while respecting QoS constraints. Evaluated on ARM big.LITTLE and Intel Alder Lake systems.

title: CGSim: A Simulation Framework for Large Scale Distributed Computing Environment
problem: Limited simulation capabilities for large-scale distributed computing environments
method: SimGrid-based simulation framework with plugin mechanisms

title: Single-Address-Space FaaS with Jord
problem: Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) systems incur millisecond-level overheads from isolating functions in separate address spaces (containers or microVMs), preventing them from meeting microsecond-scale service-level objectives (SLOs) required by microservice workloads. The address-space isolation mechanism forces costly context switches, copy-on-write, and cross-function data copies.
method: Jord co-locates functions in a single address space using hardware/software co-design for user-level in-process memory isolation that extends traditional virtual memory capabilities. Memory isolation and protection are enforced at nanosecond granularity without kernel involvement by leveraging hardware memory protection keys or equivalent mechanisms, enabling zero-copy cross-function communication. Scalable function dispatch is achieved through user-level scheduling that avoids OS-level context switches, allowing Jord to meet microsecond SLOs.

title: DeepPUFSCA: Deep learning for Physical Unclonable Function attack based on Side Channel Analysis support
problem: Physical Unclonable Functions are vulnerable to combined challenge-response and side-channel attacks, but existing machine learning attack methods do not simultaneously leverage both information sources, missing attack opportunities.
method: DeepPUFSCA combines challenge and side-channel power consumption information features during deep learning model training to attack arbiter PUFs implemented on FPGA, demonstrating that fused multi-modal information significantly amplifies attack effectiveness.

title: Run-time Energy-Efficiency Optimization for AI and HPC Workloads
problem: Power management at exascale is critical for environmental/cost impact, but most methods require deep application knowledge.
method: Runtime power manager: spectral analysis detects repetitive patterns, traces per-pattern energy, gradient-descent optimizer finds optimal GPU frequency.

title: A PulseWidth-IN-PulseWidth-Out Universal Nonlinear Processing Element for Time-Domain In-Memory Computing Systems
problem: Time-domain in-memory computing lacks efficient nonlinear operators; frequent cross-domain data transmission (analog-to-digital-to-analog) degrades energy efficiency in edge AI systems.
method: PIPO-UNPE: pulse-width IN/OUT universal nonlinear element implementing RRAM-based two-layer ReLU network in time domain; Dynamic Loss-Responsive Subset Enhancement (DLRSE) algorithm for improved function approximation; pulse-driven programmable current source; low-latency dispersion comparator VTC.

title: Mixed-Precision Performance Portability of FFT-Based GPU-Accelerated Algorithms for Block-Triangular Toeplitz Matrices
problem: Performance portability across GPU architectures with mixed-precision requirements
method: HIP-based porting of CUDA graph kernels

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of LLM-Based Reasoning for Multiobjective HPC Job Scheduling
problem: HPC job scheduling must balance multiple conflicting objectives (makespan, wait time, resource utilization, fairness). Traditional methods (FCFS, SJF) and optimization techniques fail to adapt to dynamic workloads or simultaneously optimize multiple objectives.
method: LLM-based scheduler using ReAct framework (Reason + Act): 1) Scratchpad memory tracking scheduling history, 2) Natural-language feedback for decision refinement, 3) Constraint enforcement module ensuring feasibility. Evaluation on real-world HPC workloads (7 scenarios: heterogeneous, bursty, adversarial) using OpenAI O4-Mini and Anthropic Claude 3.7. Comparison vs FCFS, SJF, Google OR-Tools on 10-100 job instances.

title: Data Race Detection through Vibe Translation
problem: Existing data race detection tools (ThreadSanitizer, Archer) for C/Fortran+OpenMP have false negatives. Translate-then-check approach using AI models offers alternative detection strategy.
method: Translate C/Fortran+OpenMP programs to Go using AI-agent natural-language prompts (vibe coding). Use Go's built-in data race detector (which uses dynamic instrumentation) on translated code. Compare accuracy vs original-language tools.

title: An Ensemble MLP-RF Model for the Prediction of DG-MOSFETs: Addressing Fabrication Process Variations
problem: Accurately predicting Double-Gate MOSFET (DG-MOSFET) electrical characteristics (drain current, gate-source capacitance, drain-gate capacitance) across process variations is time-consuming when using TCAD simulation. ML-based prediction can accelerate device characterization.
method: Ensemble machine learning model combining MLP (multilayer perceptron) regressor and RF (random forest) regressor for DG-MOSFET characteristics prediction. Model trained to predict drain current, Cgs, Cgd as functions of device and process parameters. Classification model also developed to predict channel length from unknown devices. Performance validated via MSE, RMSE, and R² metrics.
